ripDesc.bajo: Low probability of strong rip currents based on the RONMAC-UNA coastal assessment.
ripDesc.medio: Occasional or localized rip currents; stay alert during changing tides.
ripDesc.alto: High incidence of hazardous rip currents. Exercise extreme caution in the water.
ripDesc.muy_alto: Maximum hazard due to frequent, strong rip currents. High drowning risk.
ripDesc.no_visitado: Not field-surveyed (typically remote or difficult/restricted access).

swimDesc.favorable: Low rip-current risk and no severe hazards recorded; always follow local signage.
swimDesc.precaucion: Moderate waves/currents or nearby rocks/reefs. Swim only where waves break evenly and never alone.
swimDesc.peligrosa: High or very high rip currents or severe hazards (heavy shorebreak, river mouth, or dangerous wildlife).
swimDesc.desconocida: No in-person hazard survey recorded; carefully inspect ocean conditions first.

familyDesc.adecuada: Relatively sheltered bay, low rip hazard, viable vehicle access, and no high-tide cutoff risk.
familyDesc.supervision: Moderate hazard or walk-in/rough access; requires constant adult supervision and lifejackets for children.
familyDesc.no_recomendada: Not suitable for children or older adults due to strong currents, heavy surf, rocks/cliffs, or difficult access.

drawer.tideCutoffWarn: Tide alert: Risk of getting cut off at high tide.
drawer.riverMouthWarn: River mouth nearby: Shifting currents and potential wildlife.
drawer.intertidalRocksWarn: Intertidal rocks: Watch out at low tide or in breaking waves.

guide.title: How to Spot Rip Currents & Beach Safety Rules
guide.intro: Per Dr. Isabel Arozarena Llopis's methodology (RONMAC–UNA / ICT), swimmers often mistake calm gaps in breaking waves for safe zones, when they actually mark dangerous seaward rip-current channels.
guide.plumeDesc: Brownish or sandy clouds of suspended sediment pushed seaward past the surf zone.
guide.sandyChannelDesc: A narrow gap where waves break less or not at all compared to adjacent areas. Most dangerous spot!
guide.rockyChannelDesc: Gaps in submerged rocky platforms or near headlands; currents here stay fixed in the same spot.
guide.cuspDesc: Regular ridges and troughs along the sand; rip currents commonly form opposite the troughs.
rules: Always obey warning signs posted at the beach.
Avoid entering the water immediately after a heavy meal.
Observe depressions and channels at low tide so you avoid them when the tide rises.
Do not climb slippery coastal cliffs or rocky headlands.
Stay away from river mouths and sections where waves do NOT break.
Where no lifeguards are present, ask locals where it is safest to swim.
Be extra cautious at remote beaches far from medical facilities.
Never leave children unattended near the water.
Have children wear a lifejacket—it is inexpensive and saves lives.
guide.escapeTip: If caught in a rip current: stay calm, do NOT swim against it toward shore; swim parallel to the beach to exit the channel, or float until it weakens and return where waves are breaking.

about.title: Data Source & Attribution
about.text1: Cartographic data, rip-current hazard ratings, access profiles, sand colors, geomorphology, and beach uses are derived from the "Atlas de Playas de Costa Rica con Énfasis en la Seguridad" (2024) by coastal geomorphologist Dr. Isabel Arozarena Llopis (RONMAC Program, Universidad Nacional de Costa Rica) with the Costa Rican Tourism Board (ICT).
about.text2: Safety disclaimer: Coastal conditions, road access, lifeguard presence, and rip channels change continuously with tides, swells, and seasons. This tool is an informational guide and does not replace on-site observation or instructions from lifeguards and local authorities.
about.text3: Satellite imagery provided by Esri World Imagery; base maps by OpenStreetMap, CARTO, and OpenTopoMap. Web libraries: Leaflet (BSD-2) and Leaflet.markercluster (MIT).
about.text4: Software License: The application source code and web architecture are licensed under Apache 2.0. The underlying scientific research, indicators, and Atlas classifications belong to Dr. Isabel Arozarena Llopis (RONMAC–UNA / ICT) and are not licensed under Apache 2.0.
